[Current Frontend Spec](README.md) · [Visual source map](phaseui-design.md)

Display and business states are independent: stable/hover/pressed/focus/disabled describe interaction; idle/pending/succeeded/failed/offline/stale describe business. Apply only relevant states. Pending preserves reading/navigation. Success comes from receipts/business objects, never animation completion. Offline/stale views retain readable cache with explicit status rather than pretending it is fresh.

## Component behavior

**Directory items and icons.** Use native links/buttons and aria-current for the current page. Hover/focus share one three-frame effect; press responds immediately and release continues it. Execute each activation once. Selection is a persistent surface/boundary state, applied without waiting for animation. Each icon has fixed source geometry; fragments come from its body, not helper paths displayed as the base icon.

**Input and send.** Keep the native textarea DOM, selection, caret and candidate position stable. Focus uses one 2px blue outer boundary with no inner outline. Focus/submit reconstruct local border segments in three frames over 140ms; typing and caret clicks do not replay it. Cmd+Enter or Send starts durable enqueue immediately; Enter inserts a newline and IME composition never sends. Send square 160ms, arrow 420ms. A dedicated reserved aria-live line below the editor reports local enqueue; Core acceptance appears in Pending command records. Artificial data explicitly labels its simulated queue. Save/enqueue failure retains the draft, appears in the upper error area and clears pending send text. Visual restoration never means successful delivery. Disabled controls do not play faults.

**Task rows.** Table rows contain name/goal, status, update time and disclosure. Insert detail in the same table, synchronize aria-expanded and retain row-control focus when collapsing. Label loading/pending, failure and empty lists. Read Task, Execution and approval states separately instead of deriving a state machine from examples. Cancelling work is a separate business command from cancelling decoration.

**Artifact rows and dialogs.** Default to filename plus type/time/source with minimal framing or separate surface; comparison cards belong only in diagnostics. Real saving uses a native dialog and integrity verification, distinguishing saving, cancellation, failure and completion. Use native dialog or equivalent focus management: focus on open, contain Tab, close with Escape and return to the trigger. Consequential operations have explicit confirmation; decoration does not alter authorization.

**Avatars, separators and sidebar extension.** Both Master and assistant avatars use 180ms three-frame effects without changing image semantics. Structural separators trigger randomly with at most one active globally; a skipped draw produces no effect. In #62’s gallery, also try sidebar text and existing inter-button separators using temporary display layers only. Do not add unnecessary lines or move text layout/hit areas. Compare against base coverage for Master’s assessment.

## Interruption and fallback

Keep at most one effect record per control; new activity replaces the old effect and the same contact does not restart it. Restore source display and clean animations, timers and temporary nodes on leave, drag cancellation, blur, disable, unmount or motion-off. Separators also clear on scroll/resize. Temporary layers use pointer-events:none and aria-hidden, without duplicate announcements.

Reduced motion, reduced intensity, motion-off and wireframe modes suppress fault effects without replaying backlog. Selection, focus, disabled and outcomes remain clear. Frozen frames 1/2/3 verify geometry only; also test natural playback, rapid interruption and restoration after unfreezing. Stable decoration does not prevent real check, expansion-direction or value changes.

## Conversation and unified timeline (FE-04)

Thinking is enabled by default. Thinking bodies and tool-call details start collapsed and can be expanded; collapsed entries show only a summary. Turning thinking off immediately clears its presentation and memory cache. The display preference is saved per data domain.

History supports paging in both directions, message or event ID lookup, and search within the loaded window. At most 3 pages and 150 rows are resident, with 8 MiB for text and thinking and 2 MiB per expanded message. Following occurs only while already at the tail without a text selection. Sending does not force a jump; use “Go to latest messages” explicitly.

When a long reply completes, previously displayed text stays visible while content is automatically read under the final revision and current thinking preference to cover its prior length. It never shrinks to the first fragment. Failed reads retain the text and offer retry; retained preview is labelled until reconciliation, and the full body is confirmed only at final EOF.

Full copy is offered only after the loaded body reaches EOF; otherwise the action explicitly copies the loaded portion. Links require explicit address inspection and opening and allow HTTP/HTTPS only. Remote images display alt text only.

The related rail changes scope only on explicit selection; reads send no viewed/presented/read commands. The attention page provides paginated access to full original unresolved or failed messages. Copying or restoring does not resend, and restoration cannot overwrite an existing draft. Failed messages are protected from local quota eviction and cleanup; only confirmed failed records whose text has been recovered may be explicitly discarded.

When the session enters RECOVERY_BLOCKED, the client offers a confirmed “Resume session” action using the existing session/resume command and original request-receipt protocol to continue unfinished turns. Accepted messages are not resubmitted.

Message projections may include source kind, original event ID, direct related IDs, outcome, and preview availability, derived only from existing records. A saved preview is not durable success; expired previews report no final record.
